newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper overbought, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper overbought, seen consolidating.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper is expected to consolidate on Monday and may dip against a backdrop of overbought chart signals, analysts and traders said.
However, higher levels may be tested in the near term.
Aluminium is seen range-bound between $1,650 and $1,680.
COPPER - With the 14-day RSI in overbought territory at 73 percent traders and chartists were expecting a period of consolidation or even a pullback before the upside attack resumed.
On Friday prices reached near a one-year high of $2,488 a tonne.
"The charts appear positive but the unfilled gap between $2,426/33 and the very overbought situation suggests a pullback is necessary before higher levels are tested," LME broker Brandeis said.
"We believe that the market's potential is still firmly on the upside," LME player Rudolf Wolff said. They targeted levels towards $2,600.
Harry Creates of AMT said a breach of $2,490 signalled $2,500 and possibly $2,530. Creates pegged first support at $2,462, followed by $2,450.
At 0805 GMT three months copper was indicated at $2,460/65, against Friday's late London close of $2,470/73.
ALUMINIUM - Seen ranging between $1,650 and $1,680, but adopting an upside bias.
Rudolf Wolff said it remained friendly towards the metal despite technical indicators lingering in the overbought band. It was looking for a break above $1,680 with an initial target of $1,700.
At 0805 GMT aluminium was quoted at $1,663/$1,665, compared with $1,667/$1,669.
